subject.title: [优化建议] install.sh 模块化拆分以提升可维护性

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a modular installer architecture for `scripts/install.sh`, or keep the public shell installer single-file except for focused bug-driven refactors?
rationale: The request changes the architecture of a stable public setup surface, and source inspection shows the current docs, tests, and website publish workflow still assume one served script.

options.title: Sponsor a guarded split
options.body: Approve an incremental module layout only with a single generated or bundled public entrypoint plus updated website sync and installer smoke proof.

options.title: Keep focused refactors only
options.body: Use this issue as backlog context while continuing to extract or delete installer code only when tied to concrete bugs or validation improvements.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Decide that the shell installer should remain single-file to minimize helper-loading and `curl | bash` packaging risk.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a guarded split
recommendation.body: Approve an incremental module layout only with a single generated or bundled public entrypoint plus updated website sync and installer smoke proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent install-specific fixes and refactors make this the best available owner signal for the module-boundary decision.
